binaries.name: ileapp
binaries.why: Several hundred iOS artefact parsers over a file-system extraction or a backup, with a report per artefact.

install.brew: https://github.com/abrignoni/iLEAPP (not on PyPI; run ileapp.py from a checkout)

binaries.name: aleapp
binaries.why: The same for Android: app data, accounts, usage, and the protobuf-heavy newer artefacts.

install.brew: https://github.com/abrignoni/ALEAPP (not on PyPI; run aleapp.py from a checkout)
install.apt: pinned source 2026.4.1 (install.source). Its pip is the lines of the tag's requirements.txt, pinned as it pins them, but mister_skinnylegs, which names ccl_mozilla_reader and ccl_chromium_reader by an unpinned git URL that pip will not let another URL replace (ccl_mozilla_reader's head of 2026-10-27 has a pyproject.toml that does not parse). It and its dependencies are pip_after, with --no-deps, each git one at a commit: the readers at their last commit before that head, and Brotli at 1.2.1 over the readers' old bound of 1.2.0 (GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35, an out-of-bounds write in the decoder, which reads the examined profile's cache; the readers' heads now ask for 1.2.1 themselves).

binaries.name: idevicebackup2
binaries.why: A libimobiledevice tool that talks to a device and reads or restores its backups. It is declared and unused: no skill, recipe or tool of this pack runs it, and nothing here shows it opens an encrypted backup offline, which is not provided. Whether to keep it is the owner's decision.

binaries.name: heif-convert
binaries.why: Converts an iPhone's HEIC photo to JPEG or PNG, to look at it or read it with other tools; pillow-heif opens one in a script. No skill of this pack names it yet. The program is a libheif sample application (MIT, as libheif's README says); the libheif library it links is LGPL-3.0-or-later.
